linear.function_level: GroupDemeaner (within transformation): QX'QX (packed), QX'Qy; preprocess_groups' provider means
linear.inference: slice 3b (D-46), inference_pprof_py.json: test() two-sided at the median, greater, less, the size-weighted mean, 0.25 and critical 2.5 (z_raw, p_value, flag, ci_lower, ci_upper); a five-provider subset; calculate_confidence_intervals gamma and SM (indirect, direct; two-sided, greater, less); calculate_standardized_measures at the median and the mean; negative controls (reference + 0.01; level 0.94). lin-many keeps the two-sided test, gamma and two-sided SM intervals and the median measures
linear.inference_r: inference_r.json: base R from lm, as pprof_py defines each quantity: z = sign(t) qnorm of the log tail pt(|t|, df, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE), p-values, flags against qnorm(0.975), qnorm(0.95) or 2.5, limits with qt(pnorm(c), df), SM intervals and measures by provider sums; R pprof 1.0.3's test.linear_fe and SM_output.linear_fe with option.gamma.var = 'full' (X-036)
linear.lm: lm(y ~ 0 + factor(provider) + x1 + x2 + x3), provider levels sorted in the C locale; sigma, vcov, logLik, AIC, BIC, summary's t, p = 2 pt(|t|, df, lower.tail = FALSE), confint; one-sided tests at null 0.25 by pt and qt; fitted values of the first 100 rows; R^2 = 1 - RSS / sum((y - mean(y))^2); the within cross-products of the provider-demeaned features (ave) and outcome
linear.negative_controls: nudged_outcome: y + 1 in the first row of the largest provider; dropped_row: its last row removed
linear.predict: predict (DataFrame interface) for the first 100 rows; R^2 by score's formula from predict's training predictions (score's array path rejects text keys, X-034; equal to score on the numeric-key cases)
linear.summary: summary() (two_sided, level 0.95, null 0); summary(null=0.25, alternative='greater' and 'less')

linear-re.function_level: the deviance at theta = 0, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3 (pprof_py's _objective_from_state; lme4's deviance function) and its central-difference slope in tau at tau = (0.01, 0.1, 1, 10) / W~, W~ the median weight total; NumPy's summaries of spec 4a-1 §2.1 (within solution by lstsq)
linear-re.inference: slice 4a-2 (D-54) at the tight optima, every case under REML and lre-base and lre-weights under ML: pprof_py's summary (level 0.9; two_sided, greater, less), fixed_effects_table, conf_int(0.95), test (reference 0, median, mean, 0.1; greater and less at the median; critical 2.5; the first five providers), calculate_confidence_intervals (alpha; SM indirect and direct at the median, two_sided and greater) and calculate_standardized_measures (median, mean, 0); base R's t and normal tails and quantiles on lme4's tight fit (summary with n - p - m degrees of freedom, fixed_effects_table and conf_int with n - p, tests at 0 and the median from ranef(condVar = TRUE)); R pprof 1.0.3's test.linear_re and confint.linear_re(option = 'alpha') on its own lmer fit for unweighted cases for the cases without weights, offsets or a removed intercept (X-042); the negative controls' z at reference 0
linear-re.lmer: lmer(y ~ features [+ offset(o)] + (1 | provider), weights = w, REML), provider levels sorted in the C locale; fixef, vcov, sigma, theta, ranef(condVar = TRUE), REMLcrit or deviance, logLik, AIC, BIC, devcomp's pwrss, ldL2 and ussq, fitted values and predictions (re.form = NA and with the random effects) of the first 100 rows
linear-re.negative_controls: pprof_py's tight REML fit with y + 1 in the first row of the largest provider (nudged_outcome) and with that provider's last row removed (dropped_row)
linear-re.pprof_py: LinearRandomEffectModel(reml=True and False, verbose=False) at its defaults (Powell, tol_outer 1e-8); fit(X, 'y', features, 'provider', offset_var='o', weights_var='w', include_intercept) as the case sets
linear-re.tight: the root in tau = theta^2 of (4 D(h) - D(2h)) / 3, D(h) the central difference of the reference's deviance with h = 3e-3 tau (scipy brentq; R uniroot, tol 1e-14 tau), or 0 where the deviance rises from 0; pprof_py evaluated there by fit with _optimize returning that theta; lme4 by mkMerMod at it (lFormula, mkLmerDevfun)

logistic.added_providers: OI-85 (lfe-base): the two smallest provider keys left out of the fit and added back with add_providers at -17 and +17, the sixth fitted provider replaced by 0.5; measures, tests, provider tests and predictions (round 86); rows in provider-key order
logistic.glm: glm(cbind(y, n - y) ~ 0 + factor(provider) + x1 + x2 + x3, binomial, control = glm.control(epsilon = 1e-15, maxit = 200)); loglik without sum(lchoose(n, y))
logistic.inference: slice 2b at the default and tight fits: summary(test_method='lr' and 'score'), summary(null=0.25, alternative='greater' and 'less'), auc_, predict for the first 100 rows of fitted providers; with obs_id_var='patient' (lfe-clustered) robust_variances_ and summary(variance_type='robust')
logistic.iterates: fit(max_iter=k - 1) gives the state after k Newton steps, k = 1 to 5
logistic.pprof_py: LogisticFixedEffectModel(algorithm='Serbin'): default fit (max_iter=10000, tol=1e-8, bound=10, backtrack=True, screening of providers with at most 10 records)
logistic.provider_tests: slice 2c at the default fit: test() for poibin_exact (two_sided, greater, less; reference median, mean and -0.5), score (median, mean), wald (median), bootstrap_exact (seed 1); controls with the reference shifted by 0.01 and one outcome flipped; poibin-tails.json: mpmath tails at 60 digits
logistic.r_inference: glm cases: 2 (logLik(full) - logLik(reduced)), anova(reduced, full, test = 'Rao'), the Mann-Whitney AUC with rank() for Bernoulli rows, fitted values of the first 100 fitted rows; lfe-clustered: sandwich::vcovCL(full, cluster = interaction(provider, patient, drop = TRUE), type = 'HC0', cadjust = FALSE) and the beta-known variance A0 / I^2 from glm's residuals
logistic.r_standardization: Bernoulli cases: R pprof's SM_output.logis_fe (sourced at the pinned commit) on the R SerBIN fit at tol 1e-8: indirect and direct, rate and ratio, null median
logistic.r_tests: Bernoulli cases: R pprof's test.logis_fe (sourced at the pinned commit; poibin 1.6) on the R SerBIN fit at tol 1e-8: exact.poisbinom (two.sided, greater, less) and the modified score test, null median
logistic.serbin: R pprof logis_BIN_fe_prov(threads = 1, max_iter = 10000, bound = 10, backtrack = TRUE, stop = 'beta'), tol = 1e-8 (default) and 1e-13 (tight), on pprof_py's screened rows (binomial rows expanded to Bernoulli rows)
logistic.standardization: slice 2d at the default fit: calculate_standardized_measures (indirect and direct; reference median, mean, -0.5; extreme observations with 50 trials), standardized_measure (five measures; model, robust and robust_fixed_beta variances; indirect variance null and fitted), test_standardized (each measure on its automatic scale, and on others); controls
logistic.standardized_test_options: OI-84 (lfe-base, lfe-clustered): test_standardized with mean, median and numeric null values, a FixedNull with inversion and scale_only intervals, bounds none and fixed, and all of them together (round 85); rows in provider-key order

logistic-re.function_level: the Laplace deviance at four (sigma, beta) points around pprof_py's tight nAGQ = 1 optimum, each moving sigma and at most one centred coefficient by at most two standard errors (pprof_py: PIRLS over u from 0, then _laplace_deviance; lme4: the nAGQ = 1 deviance function of c(theta, beta)), with pprof_py's Richardson central differences there; the nAGQ = 0 criterion at three sigma values
logistic-re.glmer: glmer(y ~ features [+ offset(o)] + (1 | provider), family = binomial, nAGQ = 1 and 0), provider levels sorted in the C locale, at its defaults and with glmerControl(optimizer = 'bobyqa', optCtrl = list(rhoend = 1e-12, maxfun = 1e6), tolPwrss = 1e-13); vcov with use.hessian = FALSE (X-043) and its default, ranef (condVar = TRUE), logLik, AIC, BIC, devcomp's drsum, ldL2 and ussq, fitted values, predictions and residuals of the first 100 rows
logistic-re.inference: inference_pprof_py.json: pprof_py's summary (level 0.9), test (wald at references 0, median, mean, 0.1, greater and less at the median, critical 2.5, the first five providers; poibin_exact at 0, the median and greater; resampling at 0 with n_resample 20000 and seed 7), option alpha, the SM intervals (indirect and direct ratios and rates at the median for each alternative, and two-sided at the size-weighted mean given as a number, X-046), the measures at the median, the mean and 0, and profile_sigma, all on its tightened nAGQ = 1 fit; with negative controls from the flipped-provider fit
logistic-re.negative_controls: pprof_py's tight nAGQ = 1 fit with every outcome of the largest provider replaced by 1 - y (flipped_provider) and with the first row of every provider so replaced (flipped_first_rows)
logistic-re.pprof_py: LogisticRandomEffectModel(stage2=True and False, verbose=False) at its defaults (stage 1 Powell, as nlopt is absent; stage 2 Nelder-Mead; tol_outer 1e-7, tol_pirls 1e-8) and tightened (tol_outer 1e-10, tol_pirls 1e-13, max_iter_outer 20000, max_iter_pirls 200); fit(X, 'y', features, 'provider', offset_var='o', include_intercept) as the case sets
logistic-re.r_pprof: R pprof 1.0.3's logis_re (glmer with the tightened control passed through), test.logis_re, confint.logis_re (option alpha; option SM for each alternative) and SM_output.logis_re, with computeDirectExp written in R; and lme4's profile of the tightened glmer fit at zeta steps of 0.02, with confint

three-stage.golden: pprof_py tests/data/glmm_prep (R glmm.data.prep) and tests/data/three_stage (R stage 1 beta, glmer sigma, glmm.fac.hosp gamma and SRR), files checked against REFERENCE.lock
three-stage.inference: slice 2f-4a: LogisticThreeStageModel() (marginal): stage 3's gamma, posterior moments and fitted probabilities; test() exact (two_sided, greater, less), poibin_exact, resampling (seed 1); calculate_standardized_measures (indirect, direct; median, mean, -1.0); calculate_confidence_intervals (gamma; SM for both measures); sigma_sensitivity() (or its error) and profile_sigma at 0.95 and 0.9; controls: reference median + 0.01, the first event flipped (refit)
three-stage.preparation: pprof_py glmm_data_prep(data, 'Y', 'fac', 'hosp', cutoff=10); cells keyed hosp U+001F fac
three-stage.r_stage1: glm(Y ~ 0 + cell + features, binomial, epsilon 1e-15, maxit 200) on the included rows
three-stage.r_stage2: glmer(y_adj ~ 1 + (1 | fac) + (1 | hosp) + offset(stage1_offset), binomial, nAGQ = 1, bobyqa rhoend 1e-12): theta, intercept, ranef; its deviance function at the fixed points; the saturated constant
three-stage.stage1: LogisticFixedEffectModel(use_dataprep=False, screen_providers=False).fit(included rows, provider_var='cell_id'), default and tol 1e-13; offset = features @ beta (default fit)
three-stage.stage2: slice 2f-3: LogisticRandomEffectModel(provider fac, cluster hosp, offset stage1_offset, y_adj) on the pipeline's prepared data, defaults and tol_outer 1e-12 with max_iter_outer 5000: sigmas, intercept, BLUPs, the Laplace deviance there; deviance and u at three fixed points with tol_pirls 1e-14 from u = 0; controls: offsets + 0.01 and the first five events flipped (tight); ts-shuffled permutes hosp (seed 5)
three-stage.stage3: slice 2f-2: LogisticThreeStageModel() (marginal) gives beta, sigma and the start; LogisticFERandomClusterModel(tol=1e-5 and 1e-10).fit(beta=, sigma=, gamma_init=); iterates by max_iter 1 to 3; marginal log-likelihood and score at the start and at start + 0.05 (k mod 5 - 2); sigma 1e-4 and the sigma = 0 limit (Newton in numpy); controls sigma + 0.01 and one y_adj flipped; Gauss-Hermite rules from mpmath (50 digits) and numpy's hermgauss
